title: Hardship Forbearance on Rural Home Loans
content:
**Policy.** A member facing a hardship may ask, through a forbearance request stating the months wanted, to suspend monthly payments on a Rural Home Loans loan. Forbearance is granted only when the member states a hardship that interrupts the household's ability to pay — a natural disaster affecting the home, loss of employment income, serious illness, or the death of a borrower or wage earner. It further requires that the loan is in active status with at least the product's payments-made-before-forbearance number of monthly payments made since closing (monthly bills paid in full from the opening date), that the plan is no longer than the product's months per plan and that the forbearance months already used plus the plan months does not exceed the product's lifetime forbearance months. No payment is billed for the plan months, no late charge arises for them, and interest continues to accrue on principal. When the plan ends the forborne months are moved to the end of the loan, the maturity date moves out by the plan months, regular payments resume with the next due date, and escrow is re-analysed. A member who cannot resume payments at the end of a plan is referred to a loan officer.

## Evidence

- **Hardship:** the member's own statement of a qualifying hardship, given for the loan named in the forbearance request.
- **Status, payments made and months used:** the loan record and its payment history.

## Grant test

| Test | Met when |
|---|---|
| Qualifying hardship stated | natural disaster affecting the home, loss of employment income, serious illness, or death of a borrower or wage earner |
| Loan status | active |
| Payments made since closing | at least the product's figure |
| Plan length | no more than the months per plan |
| Lifetime months | months already used plus plan months no more than the lifetime figure |

*Hypothetical case:* with 3 months per plan and 6 lifetime months, a member who has used 4 months may be granted a plan of at most 2 months.

## Status changes

Active to forbearance when the plan is granted (the plan's last day is the day before the first payment due after the plan); forbearance to active when the plan ends, with the next due date the first payment due after the plan and the maturity date the old maturity date plus the plan months.
